title: Arcee, a US open source AI lab, says Chinese models are not inherently dangerous
slides: Arcee claims Chinese models aren't dangerous—but who decides safety?
The company builds open-source AI for enterprise customization.

You can now deploy Chinese models without security panic.
Test one open model yourself before believing any ban.
thread_text:
Who decides what's safe?

Arcee says Chinese open-source models are safe enough to deploy today, no panic needed.

Threat labels are a power play.

The CEO claims bans on Chinese AI hide a race for control, not real security risks.

Enterprise customization is key.

Arcee builds open-source AI so companies can adapt models without vendor lock-in or fear.

Deploy without the hype.

You can now run Chinese models in production without triggering a security meltdown—just test them.

Test one open model today.

Pick a Chinese model on Hugging Face, run a prompt, and decide for yourself—before trusting any ban.

instagram.caption:
Some Chinese AI models you can download right now are being called safe enough for business use by a US lab—no panic button required. 🧪

Arcee, an American open-source AI company, says the security warnings around these models are really about control, not code. Their CEO argues that labeling models as "dangerous" hides a power struggle over who gets to run AI. 🚫📢

Companies can now deploy a Chinese model in production without triggering a security meltdown—just test it first yourself.

Pick one open model on Hugging Face, run a single prompt, and decide: do you trust the ban or what your own computer tells you? 🤔
